decisions.statement: Every tick reads the one readout in the surplus fall group two ways for today and compares the two.
Where the day opened is Alan's sleep on the readout's own scale before the day's costs come off.
Where the day sits is the readout's reading now.
A reading below the open is a fall.
Rungs said today are read back off the notifications sent.
A notification names its rung in its own source.
A day dropping two rungs between ticks says the rung the day reached and never the rung between.
A reading that recovers and falls again says nothing the second time.
The readout and its scale and the day's reading are read on the tick rather than compiled in.
A threshold Alan moves is honoured on the next tick rather than on a deploy.
This module writes a notification.
Nothing here knows about devices.
A tick still working at the ceiling ends the process rather than leaving two ticks at once.
Enough thrown ticks in a row end the process non-zero.
One thrown tick is a store blinking.
The loop runs until stopped.
SIGTERM or SIGINT ends that loop at its next boundary.
The readout and its scale are asked of the pages system service.
The day's reading is asked of the page query service.
Code running on the workstation reaches pages data directly.

definition: the day eating into the night, told to Alan once per rung it falls
